blocks.text: How to Choose Affordable Supplements

The [choice of food supplements](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/best-biohacking-supplements-for-longevity) should be conscious. It is important to understand that the main task is to help your body be healthy. And it doesn’t have to be expensive! There are just a few supplements an average person might need daily. To spend your money wisely, remember a few rules.

items: Scientific evidence. Choose supplements whose effectiveness has been proven by systematic studies.
Cost per serving. Choosing a small jar is not always really profitable. Often, you can save money by using the quantities.

Third-party testing. Prioritize the use of products which have been independently tested for quality (USP, NSF Certified for Sport, or Informed Sport). The testing process ensures that the product is made up of the intended ingredients without any contaminants.

Ingredient quality. A high-quality supplier has a simple composition. Avoid products with proprietary blends that do not specify the exact amount of active ingredients and additives with a high number of unnecessary ingredients.

Appropriate Dosage. Remember to count your appropriate dosage. Even a high-quality product can be ineffective if you don’t keep the correct amount. Before purchasing, compare the manufacturer’s recommended dose with that used in clinical trials and do not exceed the upper safe consumption limits without consulting a professional.

blocks.text: But supplements would work only in combination with other healthy habits, such as [sleeping well](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/13-best-sleep-gadgets), workouts and stress regulation in your life. Let’s have a look at the most important and budget biohacking supplements.

blocks.text: Top Affordable Biohacking Supplements

In the [biohacking world](https://www.biohackers.world/events), there are quite a few complicated supplements, but not every one of them is needed by a person permanently. Let’s discover the most popular and best affordable supplements.
Creatine Monohydrate

If you need to increase your body’s endurance and give your muscles more pump, creatine will be a great addition to your diet. It is basically a form of carbon acid that is in our bodies and also comes from food. Creatine is one of the most extensively studied sports supplements. According to the research conducted as well as the opinion of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, [creatine helps increase muscle mass and strength](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28615996/) if used in conjunction with training.
Typical price: $5-10 monthly.
Who may benefit: athletes, elderly people, vegetarians.
Possible side effects: slight fluid retention and rare gastrointestinal discomfort.

Creatine is one of the most effective and affordable supplements due to its high efficacy and safety. It helps muscles become stronger, and also plays a key role in energy exchange by helping to replenish the cells’ main source of energy quickly.
Magnesium

If you feel that your anxiety has increased or you are sleeping poorly, magnesium will help you. It is a mineral that is vital to our body. It supports the nervous system, heart health and sufficient energy. Most beneficial for people with insufficient consumption of this mineral, and some studies also link it to [improved sleep quality](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33865376/).
Typical price: $6-12 monthly.
Who may benefit: people with magnesium deficiency, physically active adults and the elderly.
Possible side effects: high dosage might be a cause of diarrhea.
Magnesium is an affordable longevity supplement with a good evidence base, especially when proven or likely to be deficient.
Vitamin D

This vitamin plays an important role in the process of absorbing calcium, phosphorus, and in nervous system function. Vitamin D helps the body to fight against viruses and protects against diseases such as rickets and osteoporosis. Major studies show that the greatest benefit of vitamin D is seen in people with a deficiency. The [VITAL study](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1809944?utm_) did not find a universal preventive effect of high doses of vitamin D in healthy individuals with normal levels, so the addition is most justified when deficient. This benefit is especially important for those living in countries with few sunny days.
Typical price: $3-8 monthly.
Who may benefit: people with low vitamin D levels and limited sun exposure.
Possible side effects: excessive doses may cause hypercalcemia in prolonged use.
Vitamin D is one of the cheap supplements for health and can help replenish energy. It is necessary to consult with an expert to know whether you lack this vitamin.
Omega-3 Fish Oil

This is a group of polyunsaturated fatty acids. They are vital to the human body and are not produced by the body itself. That is why it is so vital for Omega-3 to arrive in our body. Usually, we obtain it through our food – fish, oil and seafood. However, if our diet contains low amounts of such elements, it may be useful to take Omega-3 as a dietary supplement. It is a substance which keeps our blood free from any fats, reduces inflammation and supports the brain, memory and eyesight. There are systematic reviews proving the effectiveness of omega-3 in lowering triglycerides. Its effect on the prevention of cardiovascular diseases varies from person to person.
Typical price: $8-20 monthly.
Who may benefit: people who rarely eat sea fish.
Possible side effects: fishy burps and mild stomach discomfort.

Omega-3 supplements are especially useful for people who eat little fish. It is a beneficial supplement that helps in supporting brain health and the vascular system. Still, nutrition is just as important for maintaining a healthy routine.
Electrolytes

These are materials that decompose into ions when coming into contact with water. The ability of electrolytes to carry electric currents is used for carrying messages from the brain to muscles and body organs. Mostly, athletes opt for electrolytes so that they do not lose too much water when engaging in sports activities. For most people, they are not a necessity, but they will be useful both during training and in high heat when there is an intense loss of moisture in the body.
Typical price: $5-15 monthly.
Who may benefit: athletes and people with high perspiration.
Possible side effects: excessive consumption of sodium.
In general, electrolytes are not required as a suppennant, but may be useful during hot seasons.
Psyllium Husk (Fiber)

The dissolving fibre from a seed shell is called psyllium. It helps to increase the consumption of dietary fibres that our digestive system needs. Sufficient consumption of fibre supports the GI function, gives a feeling of satiety and lowers LDL cholesterol levels. Also, the psyllium has a strong evidence base. Tests show that increased fibre intake is associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease and improved metabolic health. Some studies have confirmed the ability of psyllium to reduce cholesterol levels moderately.
Typical price: $5-10 monthly.
Who may benefit: people with low fiber consumption.
Possible side effects: abdominal swelling with insufficient water consumption.
Consuming enough fibre is important for our gut health and to maintain a good appearance. Psyllium helps in this and is a fairly affordable supplement.
Glycine

It is an amino acid that helps to synthesize proteins and collagen. It also participates in the functioning of the nervous system. Small clinical studies show that taking glycine before bed can [improve sleep quality](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/best-peptides-for-sleep) and reduce daily fatigue. Still, the evidence base is considerably smaller than that of magnesium or creatine.
Typical price: $6-12 monthly.
Who may benefit: people with irregular sleep patterns.
Possible side effects: rarely, a slight discomfort in the stomach.
Although it is a promising food supplement, its evidence base is still weak. At the moment, glycine is thought to help improve sleep quality.
Caffeine + L-Theanine

Caffeine is one of the most widely studied stimulants that affects our vigour and concentration. L-theanine, in turn, is an amino acid. It is predominantly contained in green tea. It has a relaxing effect without significant drowsiness. Together, they reinforce each other’s actions, increasing productivity without anxiety and eliminating nervousness. Studies show that a combination of caffeine and L-theanine can improve attention and cognitive performance compared to caffeine alone.
Typical price: $6-15 monthly.
Who may benefit: students, office workers and people with high mental stress.
Possible side effects: insomnia and anxiety in the presence of caffeine.

The combination of caffeine and L-theanine is an affordable subset that helps improve your wakefulness and focus. Still, one should take into account individual reactions to caffeine to avoid further anxiety.
Protein Powder

One of the main wellness trends is protein maxing – increased consumption of high-protein products. This trend is not just an accident. Indeed, protein is one of the most important components in our body. It helps to build muscles, recover from hard physical work and maintain immunity. But quite often, getting your daily rate right is not an easy task. In this case, protein powder helps – a concentrated product that helps regulate consumption. Studies show that protein supplements can enhance muscle mass gain and strength when combined with strength training. Often, athletes prefer protein powder, as with high loads and a lack of protein, the body begins to use muscles as a source of energy. Still, such a powder can be useful to anyone.
Typical price: $20-40 monthly.
Who may benefit: athletes, the elderly and anyone who has difficulty getting enough protein from their food.
Possible side effects: possible discomfort in people with intolerance of milk proteins and lactose.

Protein powder helps us get the protein we need and improves our body’s health and is considered as a healthy aging supplement, as it helps our muscles and body stay strong. It will be especially useful for athletes to maintain energy and muscle growth.

blocks.text: Building a Budget Biohacking Stack

If your budget is limited, you can enhance the effect of certain additions with the right combination. It is important to choose those supplements that already have a good evidence base, and do not forget to consult with a specialist, as this stack is suitable for you. Here are the main options and goals they can help to achieve.

items: Better Sleep: Magnesium + Glycine
More Energy & Focus: Caffeine + L-Theanine
Exercise Performance: Creatine Monohydrate + Protein Powder (if you have protein deficits) + Electrolytes during long workouts
Healthy Aging: Omega-3 Fish Oil + Vitamin D (if you have deficits) + Psyllium Husk
General Wellness: Magnesium + Psyllium Husk + Omega-3 (optional if you have deficits)

blocks.text: Still, it is worth noting that no amount of exercise can replace a good night’s sleep, [a healthy diet](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-diet), and regular exercise. So don’t forget about your proper healthy routine. But still, food supplements will help to make up for the necessary deficiencies and accelerate the recovery of the organism, as well as help in enhancing concentration if incorporated into your routine in the complex.
Tips for Saving Money

Sometimes it is very hard to resist another jar of pills, as we think that it will help improve our body condition. Marketing makes us buy more and spend money on things that are not worth it at all. Some supplements are placebo-based, others simply have insufficient evidence, although they are sold on websites. Here are a few tips for buying cheap supplements for health that will help you improve your body and save money.

items: Buy only supplements you need. Choose supplements that meet your goals or help fill confirmed deficiencies.
Compare the cost per serving instead of the package price. This will allow you to objectively assess which product is actually more profitable.
Choose reputable manufacturers. Give preference to brands that undergo independent quality testing and use transparent composition.
Avoid unnecessary proprietary blends. Complex mixtures with opaque dosages are often more expensive but do not have advantages over individual components.
Review your supplement routine regularly. With a change in diet, lifestyle, or test results, some supplements may become unnecessary, helping to reduce costs.
Don’t overpay for the brand. If the product contains the same active ingredients, dosage and has independent certification, a lesser-known manufacturer may be no less reliable.

blocks.text: To improve health, it is not always necessary to spend a fortune. Biohacking supplements can provide meaningful health benefits when combined with healthy habits even with little money. The main thing is a conscious and sensible approach to food supplements. Supplements can be useful for improving your productivity and focus. Don’t forget to prioritize supplements supported by quality research. If your budget is limited, pay attention to such items as:

items: Magnesium
Creatine Monohydrate
Psyllium

blocks.text: These are some of the most studied additives that will help maintain strength and energy in the body. They will also improve concentration and the nervous system. Yet they cannot substitute for regular quality sleep, nutritious nutrition, and sports discipline. These points are particularly important for the long-term outcome.
